english.title: Have on premises material ready for sale as fertiliser not marked in the manner required
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person to whom section 69(1) of the Agriculture Act 1970 applied, had material of a prescribed description, namely **(..SPECIFY MATERIAL..) on your premises for the purpose of selling it in the course of trade for use as a fertiliser, which was ready for sale and which

(A)_[was not marked in the manner required by or under section 69 of the Agriculture Act 1970]_
(B)_[was not marked with all the information or instructions referred to in section 68(1)(b) of the Agriculture Act 1970 with which it was required by that section to be marked]_
(C)_[was marked with a mark which, as respects a sampled portion of the material, did not contain all the particulars referred to in section 68(1)(a) of the Agriculture Act 1970 with which the material was required by that section to be marked]_
(D)_[was marked with a mark which, as respects a sampled portion of the material, contained particulars which were false to the prejudice of a purchaser]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 69(4) of the Agriculture Act 1970.

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale .

Time Limit on Prosecutions
six months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
